title: Forced consolidation leaves stale CSVs from previous exports
reasoning: --force reuses the existing directory, but output files are written only when their new datasets are nonempty. A subsequent export that skips rubric, quality, or evaluation processing leaves the previous files intact alongside newly written run data. Consumers can therefore read a mixture of different exports.
reproduction: Consolidate runs containing rubric and evaluation data, then consolidate a different collection into the same output directory with --force --skip-rubric --skip-evaluations. The old rubric.csv and evaluations.csv.gz remain.
recommendation: Publish a complete replacement export, or explicitly remove command-owned output files that are absent from the new export. Preserve the existing export until collection and validation succeed.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The consolidation integration test writes to a fresh directory and does not exercise repeated forced exports or datasets becoming empty.
suggestedRegressionTest: Expand the consolidation workflow test to perform successive exports with different optional datasets and verify that every retained output belongs to the latest export.
minimumFixScope: Output publication and cleanup of command-owned CSV files in consolidate_runs.
